Disputed finding 1 (intrinsic vs occurrence gate): not a real issue. In barekhu.xml (he), Psalm 113:2 sits inside a tei:seg source with its own verse milestone and no conditional, so bible:psalms/113/2 resolves with no quorum condition. The minyan gate in the expanded index covers only this occurrence of call, yitbarakh and response.

Birnbaum barekhu.xml (read in full) also defines barekhu/yitbarakh as running through ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו and יהי שם יי מבורך. The Marmorstein scope is therefore consistent with the existing shared identity. Cutting it down, as round 1 proposed, would break that consistency. Round 1's required change is withdrawn.

Call → yitbarakh → response remains an editorial reading of the concurrent columns. I confirm that no 'during' rubric was invented: none is printed and none is encoded. The documentary file keeps the printed column order: call, response, then the congregation column.

El melekh ne'eman is transcluded unconditionally and carries its own minyan=false gate. Because minyan is declared only inside the Barekhu div and ended there, quorum is undefined at El melekh ne'eman, so it prints with יחיד אומר. That is correct.

Every excerpt publication URN names the actual verse range, edition-qualified. The expanded index uses target/targetEnd point pairs (no ranged targetEnd), which satisfies the transclude schematron rule.

Disputed finding 2 (Shema Bible paragraphs): the reasoning is consistent with JLPTEI-3 ('Do not duplicate a canonical URN merely because the text is printed again elsewhere'; quotation wrappers are for bounded quotations inside composites). Pure verse ranges encoded as canonical bible URNs need no prayer:shema/* identity. Round 1's open question is withdrawn. I could not confirm the registry contents myself (see limits).
